title: Measuring a Forest's Breath
endLine: A flux tower measures net exchange; models split photosynthesis from respiration.

scenes.tts: How do you measure a whole forest's photosynthesis without sealing it inside a jar? Instead, fast sensors on a tower above the canopy watch carbon ride the wind. That method is eddy covariance.
scenes.caption: How do you measure a whole forest's photosynthesis without sealing it inside a jar? Instead, fast sensors on a tower above the canopy watch carbon ride the wind. That method is eddy covariance.
scenes.visual: A cross-section of a green forest canopy fills the lower frame under an open sky (schematic). A faint glass jar outline fades around a tree and dissolves as too small; a tall lattice tower rises above the treetops with wind curls and glowing carbon dots drifting past its top sensors.
scenes.narration: How do you measure a whole forest's photosynthesis without sealing it inside a jar? Instead, fast sensors on a tower above the canopy watch carbon ride the wind. That method is eddy covariance.

scenes.visual: Over the same forest canopy and lattice tower, schematic wind currents keep drifting past the sensors while the title 'Measuring a Forest's Breath' appears cleanly in high contrast, then clears.

scenes.tts: Fast sensors above the canopy track vertical wind and C O 2 concentration. Sinking gusts carry air into the canopy; rising gusts lift it back out. When rising gusts hold less C O 2 than sinking ones, the forest takes carbon in. Averaged yearly, that gives net ecosystem exchange, N E E.
scenes.caption: Fast sensors above the canopy track vertical wind and CO2 concentration. Sinking gusts carry air into the canopy; rising gusts lift it back out. When rising gusts hold less CO2 than sinking ones, the forest takes carbon in. Averaged yearly, that gives net ecosystem exchange, NEE.
scenes.visual: Zoom slightly toward the sensors at the top of the same tower (schematic). Downward wind arrows carry dense clusters of CO2 dots into the canopy; upward arrows emerge carrying fewer dots. A vertical gauge on the right tallies the yearly balance and settles with the label 'NEE (net exchange)'.
scenes.narration: Fast sensors above the canopy track vertical wind and CO2 concentration. Sinking gusts carry air into the canopy; rising gusts lift it back out. When rising gusts hold less CO2 than sinking ones, the forest takes carbon in. Averaged yearly, that gives net ecosystem exchange, NEE.

scenes.tts: That net combines two opposite rates. Gross primary production, G P P, is total photosynthetic fixation. Ecosystem respiration, R eco, is release from plants, animals, fungi and bacteria. Suppose the tower counts release to the air as positive. If a forest stores carbon this year, will its N E E be positive or negative?
scenes.caption: That net combines two opposite rates. Gross primary production, GPP, is total photosynthetic fixation. Ecosystem respiration, Reco, is release from plants, animals, fungi and bacteria. Suppose the tower counts release to the air as positive. If a forest stores carbon this year, will its NEE be positive or negative?
scenes.visual: On the same forest-and-tower world (schematic), a downward green arrow labeled 'GPP (fixation)' enters the canopy and an upward amber arrow labeled 'Reco (respiration)' rises from trees and soil. On the right gauge, '+' sits above zero for release to air and '−' sits below. A question card appears: 'Forest stores carbon: positive or negative NEE?'.
scenes.narration: That net combines two opposite rates. Gross primary production, GPP, is total photosynthetic fixation. Ecosystem respiration, Reco, is release from plants, animals, fungi and bacteria. Suppose the tower counts release to the air as positive. If a forest stores carbon this year, will its NEE be positive or negative?

scenes.visual: The question 'Forest stores carbon: positive or negative NEE?' stays on screen beside the forest and tower while schematic gusts keep drifting and the gauge needle gently hovers around zero.

scenes.tts: Negative. With release counted positive, N E E equals R eco minus G P P. A forest that stores carbon fixes more than it releases, so N E E falls below zero. Say a tower reads minus three hundred grams of carbon per square metre per year. Uptake beat release by three hundred: a net sink.
scenes.caption: Negative. With release counted positive, NEE = Reco − GPP. A forest that stores carbon fixes more than it releases, so NEE falls below zero. Say a tower reads −300 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹. Uptake beat release by 300: a net sink.
scenes.visual: The question clears and the gauge needle drops into the negative zone to −300 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹ (computed from the worked example). Above the canopy, the equation 'NEE = Reco − GPP' appears; the downward GPP arrow grows visibly longer than the upward Reco arrow, showing a net sink of 300.
scenes.narration: Negative. With release counted positive, NEE = Reco − GPP. A forest that stores carbon fixes more than it releases, so NEE falls below zero. Say a tower reads −300 g C m⁻² yr⁻¹. Uptake beat release by 300: a net sink.

scenes.tts: Three hundred is net exchange, not photosynthesis. A flux tower measures net exchange alone; a partitioning model splits photosynthesis from respiration. At night, photosynthesis stops, so the tower records respiration alone. Models extend night-time respiration into daytime. Adding modelled respiration to net uptake estimates G P P, which is larger than three hundred.
scenes.caption: 300 is net exchange, not photosynthesis. A flux tower measures net exchange alone; a partitioning model splits photosynthesis from respiration. At night, photosynthesis stops, so the tower records respiration alone. Models extend night-time respiration into daytime. Adding modelled respiration to net uptake estimates GPP, which is larger than 300.
scenes.visual: The sky over the same forest and tower darkens to night (schematic): the downward GPP arrow disappears, leaving only a solid upward Reco arrow measured by the tower. Daylight returns; the Reco arrow extends into the day as a dashed modelled arrow, and a dashed downward GPP arrow appears whose length equals modelled Reco plus the 300 net uptake. As the dashed GPP arrow appears, the formula 'GPP = modelled Reco + 300' writes above the canopy (schematic: the lesson gives no Reco value).
scenes.narration: 300 is net exchange, not photosynthesis. A flux tower measures net exchange alone; a partitioning model splits photosynthesis from respiration. At night, photosynthesis stops, so the tower records respiration alone. Models extend night-time respiration into daytime. Adding modelled respiration to net uptake estimates GPP, which is larger than 300.

scenes.tts: Two traps mislead. First, check the sign convention; reversing it flips uptake into release. Second, no method observes G P P directly at ecosystem scale. Besides night-time extrapolation, models use light-response fits or neural networks. Every G P P estimate carries a method attached.
scenes.caption: Two traps mislead. First, check the sign convention; reversing it flips uptake into release. Second, no method observes GPP directly at ecosystem scale. Besides night-time extrapolation, models use light-response fits or neural networks. Every GPP estimate carries a method attached.
scenes.visual: On the right gauge, the '+' and '−' labels briefly flash and lock in place with 'Check sign convention'. Over the canopy (schematic), the single dashed GPP arrow shifts through three faint model outlines labeled 'Night-time fit', 'Light-response', and 'Neural network' while the solid NEE bar stays unchanged.
scenes.narration: Two traps mislead. First, check the sign convention; reversing it flips uptake into release. Second, no method observes GPP directly at ecosystem scale. Besides night-time extrapolation, models use light-response fits or neural networks. Every GPP estimate carries a method attached.

scenes.tts: Towers now span whole networks. In 2020, a study applied a neural-network method trained on environmental drivers to thirty-six FLUXNET 2015 tower sites. It split each tower’s net flux. Yet methods can agree without being right, since none observes G P P directly.
scenes.caption: Towers now span whole networks. In 2020, a study applied a neural-network method trained on environmental drivers to 36 FLUXNET2015 tower sites. It split each tower’s net flux. Yet methods can agree without being right, since none observes GPP directly.
scenes.visual: The forest-and-tower view pulls back gently to show a schematic array of tower icons labeled '36 FLUXNET2015 sites (2020)' pulsing with net exchange bars. Two model curves align closely, then a caution tag highlights: 'Agreement is not independent validation'.
scenes.narration: Towers now span whole networks. In 2020, a study applied a neural-network method trained on environmental drivers to 36 FLUXNET2015 tower sites. It split each tower’s net flux. Yet methods can agree without being right, since none observes GPP directly.

scenes.tts: In 2022, Kukka-Maaria Kohonen and colleagues compared four G P P methods at Hyytiälä, Finland. They studied a Scots pine forest, 2013 to 2017. Two methods used C O 2 fluxes. Two used carbonyl sulfide, a gas leaves take up alongside C O 2. That gives a second route to G P P.
scenes.caption: In 2022, Kukka-Maaria Kohonen and colleagues compared four GPP methods at Hyytiälä, Finland. They studied a Scots pine forest, 2013 to 2017. Two methods used CO2 fluxes. Two used carbonyl sulfide, a gas leaves take up alongside CO2. That gives a second route to GPP.
scenes.visual: Zoom back onto a Scots pine canopy with the lattice tower, tagged 'Hyytiälä, Finland · 2013–2017 · Kohonen et al. 2022'. Beside the drifting CO2 dots, a second stream of distinct teal dots labeled 'Carbonyl sulfide (schematic)' drifts downward into the pine needles; four estimate slots appear: two labeled CO2, two labeled carbonyl sulfide.
scenes.narration: In 2022, Kukka-Maaria Kohonen and colleagues compared four GPP methods at Hyytiälä, Finland. They studied a Scots pine forest, 2013 to 2017. Two methods used CO2 fluxes. Two used carbonyl sulfide, a gas leaves take up alongside CO2. That gives a second route to GPP.

scenes.tts: Daily carbonyl sulfide estimates averaged seven or twenty-three percent above the C O 2 reference. The figure depended on the model of the two gases’ uptake ratio. The study does not say which estimate is true. Trust a flux tower for net exchange, and always name the model behind photosynthesis.
scenes.caption: Daily carbonyl sulfide estimates averaged 7% or 23% above the CO2 reference. The figure depended on the model of the two gases’ uptake ratio. The study does not say which estimate is true. Trust a flux tower for net exchange, and always name the model behind photosynthesis.
scenes.visual: The slots become bars with computed relative heights: the CO2-based reference bar sits at baseline, the second CO2 slot stays an empty outline (no value given), and the two carbonyl sulfide bars rise to +7% and +23% above it, each marked with an open question mark. The bars fade back into the single tower measuring solid NEE while the dashed GPP arrow softly pulses.
scenes.narration: Daily carbonyl sulfide estimates averaged 7% or 23% above the CO2 reference. The figure depended on the model of the two gases’ uptake ratio. The study does not say which estimate is true. Trust a flux tower for net exchange, and always name the model behind photosynthesis.

scenes.visual: The forest canopy and tower dim smoothly behind a clean centered end card displaying the exact sentence: 'A flux tower measures net exchange; models split photosynthesis from respiration.'.
